Components: Adequacy components: Total Fruits, Whole Fruits, Total Vegetables, Greens and Beans, Total Protein Foods, Seafood and Plant Proteins (0–5 points each); Whole Grains, Dairy, Fatty Acids (0–10 points each). Moderation components: Refined Grains, Sodium, Added Sugars, Saturated Fats (0–10 points each).
Scoring criteria and cut-offs: Density-based scoring per 1,000 kcal or percentage of energy. Maximum standards: Total Fruits ≥0.8 cup eq/1,000 kcal; Whole Fruits ≥0.4 cup eq/1,000 kcal; Total Vegetables ≥1.1 cup eq/1,000 kcal; Greens and Beans ≥0.2 cup eq/1,000 kcal; Whole Grains ≥1.5 oz eq/1,000 kcal; Dairy ≥1.3 cup eq/1,000 kcal; Total Protein Foods ≥2.5 oz eq/1,000 kcal; Seafood and Plant Proteins ≥0.8 oz eq/1,000 kcal; Fatty Acids, defined as (PUFA+MUFA)/SFA, ≥2.5. Moderation maximum-score standards: Refined Grains ≤1.8 oz eq/1,000 kcal; Sodium ≤1.1 g/1,000 kcal; Added Sugars ≤6.5% of energy; Saturated Fats ≤8% of energy. Minimum-score standards: no intake for adequacy food groups; Fatty Acids ≤1.2; Refined Grains ≥4.3 oz eq/1,000 kcal; Sodium ≥2.0 g/1,000 kcal; Added Sugars ≥26% of energy; Saturated Fats ≥16% of energy. Intakes between minimum and maximum standards are scored proportionately. HEI-2020 has the same 13 components and scoring standards as HEI-2015.

Components: Adequacy components: Vegetables, Fruit, Whole Grains, Nuts and Legumes, Long-chain n-3 fatty acids, Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids (0–10 points each). Moderation components: Sugar-sweetened beverages and fruit juice, Red/processed meat, Trans fat, Sodium, Alcohol (0–10 points each).
Scoring criteria and cut-offs: Higher intake receives higher scores for adequacy components, and lower intake receives higher scores for most moderation components. Common maximum-score standards include vegetables ≥5 servings/day, fruit ≥4 servings/day, whole grains ≥75 g/day for women and ≥90 g/day for men, nuts and legumes ≥1 serving/day, EPA+DHA ≥250 mg/day, and PUFA ≥10% of energy. Sugar-sweetened beverages and fruit juice, red/processed meat, trans fat, and sodium are reverse scored. Sodium is commonly scored using sex-specific deciles within the study population. Alcohol is scored as an optimal/moderate-intake component rather than a simple reverse-scored component. Intermediate intakes are scored by linear interpolation.

Components: Vegetables, Fruit, White-to-red meat ratio, Fiber, Trans fat, PUFA:SFA ratio, Calcium, Folate, Iron; 9 components, 0–10 points each.
Scoring criteria and cut-offs: AHEI-P is a pregnancy-specific modification of AHEI. Alcohol is excluded because alcohol is not recommended during pregnancy; the nuts and soy protein component is excluded; folate, calcium, and iron are added as pregnancy-relevant nutrients and are calculated from foods only, not supplements. Maximum-score standards: vegetables ≥5 servings/day; fruit ≥4 servings/day; white-to-red meat ratio ≥4; fiber ≥25 g/day; trans fat ≤0.5% of energy; PUFA:SFA ratio ≥1; calcium ≥1,200 mg/day; folate ≥600 µg/day; iron ≥27 mg/day. Minimum-score standards: zero intake for most positive components; trans fat ≥4% of energy and PUFA:SFA ratio ≤0.1 for the adverse end of fat-quality components. Intermediate intakes are scored proportionately between 0 and 10.

Components: Positive components: Fruits, Vegetables, Nuts and Legumes, Whole Grains, Low-fat Dairy. Reverse components: Sodium, Red/processed meat, Sugar-sweetened beverages.
Scoring criteria and cut-offs: Intake distributions are divided into quintiles within the study population. For positive components, quintiles Q1–Q5 receive 1–5 points. For reverse components, quintiles Q1–Q5 receive 5–1 points. The 8 component scores are summed, giving a total score from 8 to 40.

Total score range: 0–9, commonly treated as a quasi-continuous nutrient-target score
Components: Total fat, Saturated fat, Protein, Cholesterol, Fiber, Magnesium, Calcium, Potassium, Sodium.
Scoring criteria and cut-offs: Scoring is based on nutrient goals derived from the DASH dietary pattern. Each nutrient receives a score according to whether intake meets the DASH target, reaches an intermediate target, or does not meet the target. Higher scores reflect better accordance with DASH nutrient goals. The 9 nutrient scores are summed. When implemented with partial or interpolated scoring, the resulting score can be treated as continuous.

Components: Positive components commonly include vegetables, fruit, nuts, legumes, whole grains, fish, and MUFA:SFA ratio. Reverse component: red and processed meat. Alcohol is scored as a moderate-intake component.
Scoring criteria and cut-offs: For positive components, intake above the sex-specific median receives 1 point and intake at or below the median receives 0 points. For reverse components, intake below the sex-specific median receives 1 point and intake at or above the median receives 0 points. Moderate alcohol intake receives 1 point; otherwise 0 points. Component definitions differ slightly between the original Mediterranean Diet Score and aMED; if the implementation is aMED, the index name should be reported as aMED.

Components: Fourteen components including olive oil as the main culinary fat, amount of olive oil, vegetables, fruit, red/processed meat, butter/cream/margarine, sugar-sweetened beverages, wine, legumes, fish/seafood, commercial sweets or pastries, nuts, preferential consumption of poultry over red meat, and sofrito.
Scoring criteria and cut-offs: Each item is scored as 1 if the participant meets the predefined MEDAS criterion and 0 otherwise. The 14 binary items are summed. Higher scores indicate greater adherence to the Mediterranean dietary pattern.

MEDI-V2 should be described as a software-implemented continuous extension of MEDAS unless an independent scoring-method paper is identified. Each of the 14 MEDAS components is expanded from a binary 0/1 item to a 0–5 continuous or ordinal item according to intake level or degree of adherence; the 14 component scores are summed. The original MEDAS paper supports the 0–14 binary screener, not necessarily the 0–70 continuous extension.

Total score range: 0–8 for V1; V2 continuous score according to software implementation
Components: Positive components: Vegetables, Fruits, Whole Grains. Restriction or reverse-scored components: Red/processed meat, Sugar-sweetened beverages, Highly processed foods, Alcohol.
Scoring criteria and cut-offs: The score is based conceptually on the American Cancer Society 2020 guideline for diet and physical activity for cancer prevention. Higher scores indicate better adherence to the ACS dietary recommendations. For V1, components are scored using categorical cut-offs to produce a total score from 0 to 8. For V2, the same dietary domains are assigned using a continuous scoring approach according to the software implementation. Because the currently verified source is the ACS guideline rather than a separate scoring-method paper, the scoring implementation should be explicitly cited to the package/code documentation if used.

Components: Adequacy components, optimum or moderation components, and ratio/supplementary components reflecting the EAT-Lancet healthy reference diet. Typical domains include whole grains, tubers/starchy vegetables, vegetables, fruits, dairy foods, legumes, nuts, eggs, fish/seafood, meat and poultry, oils and fats, added sugars, and related proportional or ratio components.
Scoring criteria and cut-offs: PHDI quantifies adherence to the EAT-Lancet planetary health diet. Components are scored according to proximity to recommended intake targets or ranges. Adequacy components receive higher scores with higher intake up to the recommended level; moderation components receive higher scores when intake is lower or within the recommended upper limit; optimum-range components receive the highest scores when intake falls within the recommended range. In the current 16-component implementation, each component contributes up to 10 points, yielding a total score from 0 to 160.
